claim: Human concept learning of rule-based categories is well fit by Bayesian inference over short logical formulas: simple formulas are favoured, fit to data fixes the rest.
agent_test: Give the agent worked examples of a concept; compare (a) free-form description vs (b) forced shortest-formula restatement before generalising; same tokens; score held-out items.

claim: Individual people behave as if they hold one rule at a time (sharp switches), and group averages only look graded. Model with one sampled formula per person gives R2=0.83 on 36 individual patterns.
agent_test: Sample K single hypotheses and commit to each in turn instead of averaging a blended answer; compare accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: A learner over programs can show staged learning (1-, 2-, 3-, 4-knower, then a jump) from data volume alone. The timing of the jump depends on a free recursion-cost parameter and hand-picked primitives; no new child data tested it.
agent_test: Not testable on an agent directly; keep as background only.

claim: The claim that children bootstrap number by program induction is contested: Carey's analogy account and Rips et al.'s modular-number critique are not ruled out, and Lafond et al. (2007, snippet only) found shortest-formula length does not fully predict difficulty. Update: Feldman 2000 abstract confirmed (41 concept types, 6 families, difficulty proportional to shortest-formula length); Lafond 2007 still unverified.
agent_test: None; do not build on the number-word result.

claim: An LLM that proposes hypotheses (as text or code) and a checker that tests them on the examples beats direct answering. GPT-4 on ARC 17% direct to 30% with summarised hypotheses; 1D-ARC 39.6 to 73.1; List Functions 31 to 69. Qiu et al. ACRE task accuracy 28 to 59, MiniSCAN 0 to 70, List Functions 39.6 to 52.4. Exception: MiniARC got worse (IO 13.8 vs 14.6 best refinement, 3.8-9.2 for small budgets). Update 2026: with o4-mini (a reasoning model) a propose-code-run-feedback loop reaches 55.17 on ARC-AGI-1 100-puzzle val (2 attempts); small open models with 6k samples plus refinement beat much larger one-shot models (SOAR). No study found that compares it with plain extended reasoning at equal tokens.
agent_test: Arm A direct answer; arm B propose-K-hypotheses, run each on the examples with an executable or explicit check, pick survivor; equal total tokens; ARC-like and list-function items.

claim: Writing a program instead of the answer grid already helps on exact-computation tasks (ARC 17 to 23, 1D-ARC 39.6 to 61.1, List Functions 31 to 59). Transduction (predict output directly) wins on fuzzy perceptual concepts; an ensemble of both is best (56.75% ARC validation vs average human 60.2%). Update: induction-first, transduction-fallback ensemble is a free router; refinement lost on MiniARC (raw 33.1 IO vs 5.9-12.8).
agent_test: Route per item: try program route first, fall back to direct prediction; compare with either alone at equal tokens.

claim: The natural-language hypothesis step helps only when the concept is hard to state as code. On SyGuS string tasks hypotheses add nothing (94.3% both ways); language-only hypotheses without coding gave 19%, below 23% for programs alone.
agent_test: Add the language step only for items where a first code attempt fails; measure the gain by item type.

claim: Hypothesis generation, not coding, is the main bottleneck: GPT-4 produced a correct hypothesis for only 49 of 100 ARC tasks, and 33 of those 49 (67%) ended correct. Human-written hypotheses lift ARC to 45%.
agent_test: Spend more of the budget on diverse proposals than on debugging one; test at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs are good at proposing rules but poor at applying them: MiniSCAN task accuracy about 85-93% with a symbolic interpreter vs 0.0% when the LM applies its own rule; GPT-4 alone gives judgements unlike humans on the number game and scores below the Bayesian wrapper on shape concepts. Update: executing in code removes the LM-as-interpreter failure; remaining raw-task gap on ACRE (78.2 vs 45.0 at T=1,N=1) reflects wrong rules plus a strict metric.
agent_test: Same induced rule applied by (a) code execution, (b) the model in prose; compare error rate.

claim: More sampled programs raise the solve rate almost monotonically; sampling thousands of programs per task plus debugging reached 42% on public ARC with GPT-4o. Update: Greenblatt GPT-4o adds about 3 points per doubling up to 2048 samples; Lee 2025 GPT-4o-mini average accuracy rises 36.1 (K=4) to 55.0 (K=256), only +0.6 from 128 to 256. No sharp knee found, but returns are logarithmic.
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs number of proposals at fixed total tokens; find the knee.

claim: Programs that fit all examples can still be wrong: about 9% of passing samples give a wrong test output (half still have the right majority answer). Selecting by fit to the given examples alone overfits (MiniSCAN T=3,N=1 beat N=5 in one setting). Update: Li et al. 9% is for fine-tuned 8B models; about half of affected problems are fixed by majority vote over passing programs. No modern-model rate found.
agent_test: Add a held-out example check or majority vote over passing programs; measure false-accept rate.

claim: Iterated library learning helps in controlled domains (DreamCoder text editing 3.7% to 79.6% solved; LILO beats DreamCoder by +33.14 REGEX, +20.42 LOGO) but its value for LLM agents is contested: LLM-written abstractions were only 19.01% valid, unnamed abstractions hurt (-30.60 REGEX) until auto-documented, and re-analysis found learned functions almost never reused (6% of lemmas used, one reused once; TroVE 3 reuses in 3,201). Update: ArcMemo (concept memory in prose, o4-mini) +4.2 points official at standard compute, advantage shrinks with compute, tokens not reduced; Berlot-Attwell shows 3 reuses in 3,201 TroVE questions and 1 reuse in LEGO-Prover logs. So literal code reuse stays near zero while prompt-level concept hints give small gains.
agent_test: Store solved-item abstractions with names and docs; test reuse rate and gain on a later batch at equal tokens.

claim: Humans do much better than machines on ARC-type induction: 83.8% per task (N=95, 40 tasks); ConceptARC humans about 91% vs GPT-4 25% and best program 52%; best 2024 AI ensemble 56.75% vs average human 60.2%.
agent_test: Use as headroom benchmark: report agent score against the human mean.

claim: Representation of the input matters a lot: object-based description lifted GPT-4 from 13/50 to 23/50 on simple ARC tasks; random token alphabets cut text-davinci-003 from 85 to 44-46 solved. Update: no test on 2025-26 reasoning models; the only support is GPT-4-era and an uncontrolled survey remark.
agent_test: Give the agent an object/structure parse of the problem as its S2 step vs raw text; equal tokens.

claim: LM rule induction is brittle to noisy examples and unfamiliar symbols, unlike humans (12.5/25/50% perturbed outputs lowers accuracy steadily).
agent_test: Insert a noise-tolerant fit step (allow k exceptions) and compare.

claim: Revising programs with metaprograms fits human list-function learning with far less search; Codex with one function per trial matched only 25th-percentile humans (392 humans, 100 functions; mean acc 0.521).
agent_test: Compare blind resampling vs targeted revision of the failing hypothesis at equal tokens.

claim: Generating a list of K distinct concepts first, then a hypothesis per concept, raises accuracy by +3.3 to +5.0 points over IID sampling. Update: scaling table shows gain +3.6 to +4.5 at K=4-16, +2.4 at K=32 (+6.6 with 16x2 split), +0.3 at K=128, +4.8 at K=256; tokens for concept proposal not counted. Weak models only.
agent_test: Diversity prompt vs repeated sampling at equal tokens.

claim: Hybrid execution (code run by interpreter, only unrunnable lines simulated by the model) lifts BIG-Bench Hard: text-davinci-003 CoT 72 to 84 (GPT-4 CoC 91).
agent_test: Code-with-simulation vs pure chain of thought on computable sub-steps.

claim: Translating language into probabilistic programs and letting the program engine reason is shown only qualitatively; no measured accuracy gain exists in these sources.
agent_test: Needs a benchmark first; skip.

claim: A learned rule library from training examples (Hypotheses-to-Theories) gives +10-30% over CoT; wrong rules are the failure mode.
agent_test: Rule library from earlier items vs none, equal tokens; track bad-rule rate.

claim: Reasoning models plus a propose-code-and-execute loop are strong on ARC-AGI-1, but no source compares it with plain extended reasoning at equal tokens. Same-harness numbers: o4-mini 55.17 and Claude Sonnet 4 thinking-16k 54.17 (2 attempts, 100-puzzle val); direct-grid leaderboard o3-high 60.8% at $0.50, Sonnet 4 thinking-16k 40% at $0.366, o4-mini 58.7% at $0.406.
agent_test: Run both arms on the same 50 items with token logs; K = 1, 4, 8 proposals each with execution check.

claim: Accuracy vs number of proposals has no sharp knee up to K=256 (log-like). Diversity prompting pays at small K (4-32) and vanishes near K=128 on GPT-4o-mini; refinement beats pure sampling at the same budget. Tokens for verification and for the concept stage are not reported.
agent_test: K-sweep 2, 4, 8, 16 with and without concept-first diversity at equal tokens; stop per item once a program passes all demos.

claim: A hypothesis that fits the examples is wrong on the held-out case about 9% of the time (fine-tuned 8B models, ARC-like data); majority vote over passing programs clears about half of those problems. No measurement exists for 2025-26 prompted models.
agent_test: Hold out one demonstration from selection; compare with majority vote over passing programs.

claim: Greedy single-attempt program writing is weak even for strong models (GPT-4.1 8.0, Claude-4-Sonnet 20.75, o3-mini 38.25 on ARC-test); all of the benefit comes from search and execution feedback, not from the program format alone.
agent_test: Always pair code proposals with a run-and-check step.

claim: Cost headline of the 2025 ARC leaderboard is mostly fewer parallel samples: o3 low-efficiency 1,024 samples at 5.7B tokens per 100 tasks gives 87.5%; 6 samples at 33.5M tokens gives 75.7%. All paradigms lose 2.5-3x on ARC-AGI-2 (Berman 79.6 to 29.4, Pang 77.1 to 26.0).
agent_test: Report accuracy with token count; expect large drop on harder item sets.

claim: A named-abstraction memory helps a later batch only modestly (ArcMemo +4.2 points official, shrinking with compute) and literal reuse is rare in LLM code and prover libraries (3 reuses in 3,201 TroVE questions). The LILO vs Berlot-Attwell conflict is partly a difference in what counts as reuse (function call vs idea hint).
agent_test: Log reuse rate (verbatim and idea-level) plus a no-memory control on a later batch.

claim: No LLM study was found that uses the human one-rule-at-a-time finding (Goodman 2008, Piantadosi 2016) to choose between committing to one sampled hypothesis and blending several. The nearest evidence is hypothesis-then-vote selection (Li, Greenblatt).
agent_test: Compare committing to the best-passing program vs blending answers by vote; gap not closed.

claim: Whether shortest-formula length predicts LLM difficulty is untested in the sources found. Feldman 2000 abstract: 41 types, 6 families, difficulty proportional to Boolean complexity; Lafond 2007 could not be retrieved.
agent_test: Score Boolean-concept items by minimal formula length and plot model accuracy against it.
